Fit a Dataset's Gaps From Its Own Complete Plots

Source: R/gap_fitting.R
resolve.fit_gaps.Rd

A dataset usually records a variable on most of its plots and lacks it on some. Gap fitting chooses, on the plots that carry it, how to combine the model's raw prediction with the dataset's own neighbours, and applies that choice to the plots that lack it (the gaps). The candidates are the complete plots' centre (local_constant), the raw prediction (resolve), the raw prediction calibrated by least squares (offset_slope), the median of the k most similar complete plots in species composition (knn_species) or the k nearest by great-circle distance (knn_spatial), and the raw prediction combined with those medians by least squares (stack_species, stack_species_spatial).

Usage

resolve.fit_gaps(
  raw,
  recorded,
  species,
  scale = "linear",
  period = 360,
  coordinates = NULL,
  years = NULL,
  gapFitting = NULL,
  name = "",
  folds = NULL
)

Arguments

raw

The model's prediction per plot in the target's units: a numeric vector, or for scale = "geographic" a plots x 2 matrix of latitude and longitude. NA marks a plot the model did not impute: it is neither a gap nor a complete plot.

recorded

The dataset's recorded value per plot, shaped as raw; NA marks a gap.

species

A plots x species numeric matrix; an entry other than 0 marks a species present.

scale

How the values lie: "linear", "log" (fitted on log1p), "circular" (a bearing with full turn period) or "geographic".

period

A bearing's full turn, in the target's units ("circular").

coordinates

NULL or a plots x 2 matrix of latitude and longitude (NA where unknown): the spatial axis.

years

NULL or each plot's survey year (NA where unknown).

gapFitting

NULL for the defaults, or a list of settings: candidates (method names), k_grid (the neighbour counts k is chosen from, default 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50), spatial (FALSE reads composition only), matching_seed, n_folds (default 10), max_fold_share (the largest share of the complete plots one fold may hold, default 0.5) and matching_sample (complete plots the layouts are compared on, default 1000).

name

The target's name, as the report states it.

folds

NULL, or an integer fold per complete plot (a plot with both recorded and raw; in plot order, numbered from 0) replacing the matched layout (to reproduce another implementation's layout).

Value

A resolve_gap_fit list: fitted (as raw; a plot recording the value keeps it, a plot lacking it that was not imputed is NA), method (per plot, "recorded" for a plot recording the value, "not_imputed" for one lacking it whose raw is NA) and report (n_complete, n_gaps, n_not_imputed, the gaps' distance per axis, the fold layout, the k chosen per neighbour kind, and per group of gaps every candidate's cross-validated error, the estimated error of the whole choice, the same error per held-out fold (fold_error, over fold_n_estimated complete plots) and the chosen method's coefficients).

Details

Each candidate is judged by cross-validation over the complete plots, with folds laid out to hold plots out the way the gaps are held out (k-fold nearest-neighbour distance matching, Linnenbrink et al. 2024): squares of an equal-area plane, survey-year periods, both, or plot by plot, the last also with buffers drawn from the gaps' distances, whichever leaves the held-out plots as far from the rest, in species similarity, in km and in survey years, as the gaps are from the complete plots. Every fitted part (k, least-squares coefficients) is fitted on the other folds, and the candidate with the lowest out-of-fold error, by the target's own error (mean absolute error; on a log scale that of log1p; the circular error of a bearing; the median km of a location), predicts the gaps. The whole choice, repeated with each fold held out, gives the error reported for it (estimated_error, nested cross-validation). Gaps with and without coordinates choose apart. The raw prediction is never replaced: the fitted values come back beside it.

Undated plots that are probably older than the dated ones, and plots without coordinates that probably come from an area with no georeferenced plots, are better served by the raw prediction: the complete plots cannot show how far off such gaps are.

See also

resolve.predict.suite() with gapFitting, which fits a suite's targets after combining them.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
raw <- runif(n, 1950, 2020)
recorded <- 1990 + 0.5 * (raw - mean(raw)) + rnorm(n, 0, 2)
recorded[sample(n, 60)] <- NA
species <- matrix(rbinom(n * 20, 1, 0.2), n, 20)
fit <- resolve.fit_gaps(raw, recorded, species, name = "year")
fit$report$groups$unlocated$method
table(fit$method)
